news_checked: 2026-09-27 (company IR / SEC filings; secondary sources labelled)
distortion_note: Normalized EBITDA is Yahoo's own row that strips unusual items; the report recomputes EV/EBITDA on it for every name, using the same EV (market cap + latest-quarter debt − cash) as the pipeline. GOOG's TTM includes roughly $149B of gains on equity securities; Salesforce's own Q2 FY27 release says gains on strategic investments added $2.43 to its $4.29 GAAP EPS. Changing the pipeline itself is a methodology decision — proposed in docs/agent.md, not applied.
overview_note: Read with care: four of the five are software, and three of those (ADBE, INTU, CRM) are exactly the names the 2026 market has been de-rating on AI-disruption fears. Cheapness here is concentrated in one theme, not spread across sectors. The tier also contains no energy or utilities names at all (pool-wide percentile scoring favours asset-light, high-ROIC businesses).
method_notes:
• Quality: six-metric 0–100 score (ROIC 25%, FCF margin 20%, cash quality 15%, leverage 15%, EBITDA growth 15%, revenue growth 10%), percentile-ranked across the whole pool. Source: quality pipeline, annual statements.
  • EV/EBITDA (norm.): computed in this report from the valuation pipeline's quarterly files; reported is the pipeline's own figure. P/E is TTM on reported net income, so it carries the same gains distortion (GOOG and CRM P/E look cheaper than their operations).
  • Forward P/E is Yahoo's analyst consensus (next twelve months): it moves with revisions and is not audited.
  • Technical: TradingView-style vote of 10 moving averages + 6 oscillators on daily closes. Momentum only — not a view on the business.
  • Peers are limited to companies in the screened universe (25 largest per sector, USD reporters). Several natural competitors — Paychex, Workday, Canva, Figma, H&R Block, Amazon — are not in it, so peer comparisons are partial.
  • Quarterly charts show at most five quarters (what Yahoo returns), so year-over-year growth is available only for the latest quarter.
  • Palette: the three documented-validated categorical slots (blue, orange, aqua); the palette validator could not be run locally (no Node in the container).

ADBE.name: Adobe Inc.
ADBE.industry: Software — Application (creative, document and marketing software)
ADBE.peer_caveat: Peers from the universe. Adobe's most direct creative-tool competitors (Canva, Figma, generative-AI image/video tools) are not in the screened universe.
ADBE.peer_note: Against the universe's large application-software names, Adobe has the highest ROIC (45%) and FCF margin (39%) of its peer set and the lowest valuation (9.4× normalized EV/EBITDA, 8.5× forward P/E versus 14.6–27× for CRM, NOW and MSFT). Its revenue growth (+13% in the latest quarter) is in line with CRM and INTU, behind NOW (+24%) and MSFT (+18%). So the gap is not explained by weaker current numbers: the market is pricing a risk that doesn't appear in trailing statements — that generative-AI tools erode Creative Cloud's pricing power. The case for Adobe over its peers is that you pay the least for the highest current returns on capital; the case against is that its peers' businesses (CRM/NOW workflows, MSFT platforms) are seen as less directly exposed to AI substitution.
says: Quality 75.5 (Top 25%) driven by 45% ROIC and 39% FCF margin; net cash (net debt/EBITDA −0.06).
Cheapest name in the top-quality tier: 9.4× EV/normalized EBITDA; reported and normalized EBITDA agree, so no gains distortion.
Revenue still growing: FY2025 $23.8B (+10.5%), latest quarter +13% YoY.
Price −35% over 12 months (the high, 360, was a year ago); 22% above its 25 Jun low of 193 but below both 50- and 200-day averages; Strong Sell on momentum.
means: The market is discounting a future the trailing numbers don't yet show — a terminal-value question, not a current-earnings one.
Buybacks at these prices retire more shares per dollar (9.5M shares repurchased in Q3 FY26).
The CEO handover on 1 Dec 2026 is to an internal candidate (the head of the Customer Experience business), which suggests continuity rather than a strategy reset.
uncertain: Value-trap risk is real: if AI tools compress seat pricing, today's 39% FCF margin is the peak, and a low multiple on peak margins is not cheap.
ARR growth figures differ across sources (10.2% vs 11.2%); only the $27.50B ARR level is verified here.
The downtrend has not turned: the stock fell after a beat-and-raise quarter, so good results alone are not changing sentiment.
Leadership transition adds execution uncertainty for 2027 planning.

INTU.name: Intuit Inc.
INTU.industry: Software — Application (TurboTax, Credit Karma, QuickBooks, Mailchimp)
INTU.peer_caveat: Peers from the universe. Direct competitors (H&R Block, Xero, Block) are not in the screened universe; ADP is the closest small-business-services comparison.
INTU.peer_note: Intuit grew faster than ADBE, CRM and ADP last year (+14% FY2026, the fastest of that group apart from NOW) and trades at 10.4× normalized EV/EBITDA and 10.2× forward P/E — second only to Adobe as the cheapest here — about two-thirds of ADP's EV/EBITDA and half its forward P/E. Its ROIC (17%) is lower than ADBE's or ADP's, a legacy of the Credit Karma and Mailchimp acquisitions. What separates it from peers is the guided slowdown: FY2027 revenue +9–10%, with TurboTax at only +2–3% and Mailchimp flat to down. The bull case over peers is that the small-business side (Global Business Solutions, guided +13–14%) is now the larger engine and is priced as if it were TurboTax. The bear case is that both tax prep and SMB bookkeeping are the workflows most exposed to AI agents.
says: Quality 71.6 (Top 25%): FCF margin 35%, 4-yr revenue CAGR 14%, EBITDA CAGR 21%.
10.4× EV/normalized EBITDA — slightly cheaper than reported, because the last quarter includes a −$397M unusual charge.
Price −60% over 12 months; back within 9% of its 25 Jun low (254) after September's fall; RSI 29.6 (oversold); Strong Sell on momentum.
September alone: 359.30 (31 Aug) → 275.79 (25 Sep), −23%, spanning the 17 Sep Investor Day.
means: The FY2027 guide (9–10% growth) resets expectations from a 14% grower — part of the de-rating is fundamental, not only sentiment.
Oversold RSI means the selling has been intense; it does not mean the trend has turned (MACD is still below its signal).
Capital return is aggressive ($5.5B repurchased in FY2026, dividend +15%), which supports per-share numbers at lower prices.
uncertain: Value-trap flag: consumer tax prep growth near 2–3% plus AI-agent substitution risk could make today's multiple a fair price for slower growth.
From FY2027 Intuit's non-GAAP figures include stock-based compensation, so non-GAAP comparisons across the change need care.
Quarterly figures are heavily seasonal (the April quarter carries tax season) — quarter-to-quarter comparisons in the chart are not meaningful.
Investor-day reaction reported by secondary sources only (e.g. Quiver Quantitative: 'reaffirmed a slower growth outlook'); the 10 MB presentation could not be read here.

news.text: FY2026 revenue $21.4B (+14%), GAAP EPS $16.46 (+20%); $5.5B repurchased. FY2027 guidance: revenue $23.28–23.51B (+9–10%); TurboTax +2–3%, Credit Karma +11–13%, Global Business Solutions +13–14%, Mailchimp −1% to flat; Q1 FY27 revenue +11%.

ADP.name: Automatic Data Processing, Inc.
ADP.peer_caveat: ADP's real competitors (Paychex, Workday, Paycom, Paylocity) are not in the screened universe; the peers shown are the nearest business-software names that are.
ADP.peer_note: ADP is the steady name of the five: 7% revenue growth, very high ROIC (57%) and a modest decline (−7% over a year, versus −35% and −60% for ADBE and INTU; Neutral technical rating). It is cheaper than its high-growth software peers (15.6× vs NOW at 41.8×) but more expensive than ADBE and INTU, and its growth is the slowest in the set. Against ORCL — the only other HR-software vendor in the universe — ADP's balance sheet is far stronger (Oracle's FCF margin is negative on its AI capex and leverage 3.9× net debt/EBITDA). ADP is here because it is a quality compounder at a reasonable price, not because it is deeply discounted; it looks better than peers on predictability, worse on growth.
says: Quality 66.0 (Top 25%), ROIC 57%, low leverage (net debt/EBITDA 0.35).
15.6× EV/normalized EBITDA, P/E 23.7, forward P/E 19.7 — the richest of the five.
FY2026 (June year-end) revenue $21.9B (+7%); latest quarter +7% YoY.
Price −7% over 12 months, near its 50-day average; Neutral.
means: The market is not treating ADP as an AI casualty the way it treats ADBE/INTU — its moat (payroll compliance, PEO, client-fund float) is operational rather than per-seat.
FY2027 guide (+5–6% revenue, adjusted EPS +9–11%) is a mid-single-digit grower with margin expansion — bond-like, not a re-rating story.
uncertain: Interest-rate sensitivity: client-fund interest was $1.4B in FY2026 (+14%) on $40.4B average balances; falling rates would cut high-margin revenue.
Employment sensitivity: U.S. pays per control grew only 1%, retention flat at 92.1% — slower hiring shows up directly in revenue.
ROIC of 57% partly reflects that client funds sit outside invested capital — it overstates what a new competitor could earn, but that is ADP's actual economics.
Least 'cheap' of the five: it only makes the list because EV/EBITDA ranking favours low-debt, steady earners.

news.text: FY2026 revenue $21.9B (+7%, +6% organic constant currency), diluted EPS $10.94 (+10%), adjusted EBIT margin 26.8% (+80bp); Employer Services new business bookings $2.2B (+6%), retention 92.1%. FY2027 outlook: revenue +5–6%, adjusted EBIT margin +70–90bp, adjusted EPS +9–11%.

CRM.name: Salesforce, Inc.
CRM.industry: Software — Application (CRM, customer-service and data platforms)
CRM.peer_caveat: Peers from the universe. Workday and HubSpot are not in it.
CRM.flag: Gains distortion: 21% of Salesforce's reported TTM EBITDA is unusual items, mostly gains on strategic investments (the company states they added $2.43 to Q2 FY27 GAAP EPS of $4.29). On normalized EBITDA it is 17.3×, not the pipeline's 13.6×, and its P/E of 19.9 is flattered in the same way.
CRM.peer_note: Salesforce is growing at about the same rate as Adobe and Intuit (+11% revenue, cRPO +14%) but has much lower returns on capital: 8% ROIC against 45% at ADBE and 25% at MSFT, because goodwill and intangibles from acquisitions are $65.4B of its $109.6B total assets. Against NOW, the closest workflow-platform peer, CRM grows more slowly (11% vs 24%) but costs well under half as much (17.3× vs 41.8× EV/EBITDA; 14.6× vs 27× forward P/E). The argument for CRM over peers is that margin expansion (34% non-GAAP operating margin) is converting into cash at a discount to NOW and MSFT; the argument against is lower capital efficiency and a balance sheet that now carries $41.7B of debt.
says: Quality 69.7 (Top 25%) — but the score leans on cash metrics (FCF margin 31%) rather than ROIC (8%).
17.3× EV/normalized EBITDA (13.6× reported); forward P/E 14.6.
Revenue $41.5B FY2026 (Jan year-end), latest quarter +11% YoY; FY2027 guidance raised to $46.1–46.4B.
Price −3% over 12 months but above both moving averages; Buy on momentum.
means: Unlike ADBE/INTU, CRM's price has stabilised and turned up — the market may be giving credit for margin expansion and the raised guide.
Much of the headline EPS jump (+119% GAAP) is investment gains; operating income was essentially flat quarter on quarter ($2.43B vs $2.43B).
uncertain: 8% ROIC is low for a 'quality' name; the Top-25% placement is sensitive to the cash-quality and FCF weights.
Total debt $41.7B at the latest quarter (goodwill-heavy balance sheet) — leverage on normalized EBITDA is materially higher than the quality pipeline's 4-year average suggests.
Same AI-disruption debate as other seat-based software; CRM has so far been punished less.

news.text: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended 31 Jul): revenue $11.3B (+11%), cRPO $33.5B (+14%), GAAP operating margin 20.5%, non-GAAP 34.1%; GAAP EPS $4.29 of which $2.43 from gains on strategic investments. FY27 revenue guidance $46.1–46.4B (+11–12%); Q3 revenue guidance $11.42–11.50B.

META.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
META.peer_caveat: Peers from the universe. Amazon (ads), Snap and Pinterest are not in it.
META.flag: EBITDA flatters capex-heavy companies: Meta's Q2 2026 capex was $31.08B and free cash flow only $0.78B (vs $8.55B a year earlier). EV/EBITDA ignores that spending; on free cash flow Meta is not cheap right now.
META.peer_note: Meta is the fastest grower of the five by far (+28% revenue in Q2) and, among the ad-driven platforms, cheaper than Google on normalized numbers (17.7× vs 23.8× EV/EBITDA; 21.5× vs 22.9× forward P/E) and roughly level with Microsoft (18.7×). GOOG looks cheaper on the pipeline's reported numbers only because of its securities gains. Against AppLovin (the other ad-tech name in the tier), Meta is growing more slowly (+28% vs +53%) at a similar EV/EBITDA, but with far larger scale and a much less extended share price. What makes Meta 'better' in this screen is growth at a peer-level multiple; what makes it riskier is that nearly all of its operating cash flow is currently going into AI infrastructure, so owners are paying for a capex bet.
says: Quality 77.2 (Top 25%): ROIC 24%, revenue CAGR 20%, EBITDA CAGR 41%.
17.7× EV/normalized EBITDA, forward P/E 21.5; revenue +28% YoY in Q2 2026.
Price flat over 12 months but +22% above its 50-day average; RSI 71.4 (overbought); Strong Buy on momentum.
Q2 GAAP operating margin fell to 31% from 43%; net income down 14% YoY.
means: The only one of the five where cheapness and momentum agree — but the RSI says the recent move is stretched.
Revenue is accelerating while margins compress: the market is currently rewarding growth over near-term cash.
uncertain: Capex: 2026 capex guided at $130–145B; if returns on that spend disappoint, trailing EBITDA overstates owner earnings.
Q2 included $2.40B of legal charges; Reality Labs lost $4.62B in the quarter.
Entry point: an overbought reading after a sharp run is where momentum signals most often mean-revert.
